scenes.title: The Boundary Conditions of Finance: Option Bounds
scenes.purpose: Before applying complex pricing models, option prices must satisfy model-independent boundaries
takeaways: Before applying complex pricing models, option prices must satisfy model-independent boundaries
If market prices violate these bounds, pure risk-free arbitrage opportunities arise immediately
Part 1 explores the 6 pricing factors, upper bounds, portfolio dominance, and lower bounds

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Before quantitative finance introduces complex stochastic models such as Black-Scholes-Merton or Binomial Trees, a fundamental question arises: Can we establish rigorous, absolute price boundaries for options without making any assumptions about probability distributions? The answer is an emphatic yes.

hi.display: Black-Scholes-Merton model aur Binomial Trees jaise complex valuation formulas ko study karne se pehle ek fundamental question puchhiye: Kya bina kisi complex mathematical model ke bhi hum option prices ke absolute maximum aur minimum boundaries establish kar sakte hain? Answer hai: Absolutely yes.

beats.onScreenIntent: The Boundary Conditions of Finance: Option Bounds

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: These unbreakable mathematical laws are No-Arbitrage Option Bounds. If market prices ever trade outside these boundary conditions, trading desks can execute immediate, risk-free arbitrage that guarantees positive profits.

hi.display: Ye unbreakable financial laws kehlate hain: No-Arbitrage Option Bounds. Ye bounds pure market logic aur no-arbitrage principle par base hote hain: agar market mein koi option in bounds ke bahar trade karta hai, toh instant risk-free arbitrage execute hota hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: The Boundary Conditions of Finance: Option Bounds

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: In Part One of Chapter Eleven, we will analyze the Six Fundamental Pricing Factors, derive the upper bounds for calls and puts, master the Portfolio Dominance method to prove lower bounds, and construct the exact cash-and-carry arbitrage strategies that enforce market equilibrium.

hi.display: John C. Hull ke Chapter Eleven Part One mein hum Option prices ko drive karne wale Six Factors, Call aur Put ke Upper Bounds, aur Portfolio Dominance proof ke through Lower Bounds ko second-by-second master karenge.

scenes.title: The Six Fundamental Factors: Sensitivity Matrix
scenes.purpose: Stock price increases call value (+) and decreases put value (-)
takeaways: Stock price increases call value (+) and decreases put value (-)
Strike price decreases call value (-) and increases put value (+)
Volatility strictly increases both call and put values (+, +)

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: In Table 11.1, John C. Hull formalizes the six core market variables that determine the fair economic value of any stock option: Current Stock Price S_0, Strike Price K, Time to Expiration T, Volatility of Stock Price sigma, Risk-Free Interest Rate r, and Expected Dividends D.

hi.display: John C. Hull Table eleven point one mein options pricing ke chhe fundamental drivers summarize karte hain: Spot Price S zero, Strike Price K, Time to Expiry T, Volatility sigma, Risk-free Rate r, aur Dividends.

beats.onScreenIntent: The Six Fundamental Factors: Sensitivity Matrix

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: An increase in stock price S_0 increases call values and reduces put values. A higher strike price K reduces call values and increases put values. Longer time to expiration T unambiguously increases the value of American options by expanding early exercise optionality.

hi.display: Spot Price badhne se Call option ki value badhti hai jabki Put ki value girti hai. Strike Price badhne se Call ki value girti hai jabki Put ki value badhti hai. Expiration Time badhne se American options ki value hamesha badhti hai kyunki flexibility expand hoti hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: The Six Fundamental Factors: Sensitivity Matrix

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Higher risk-free interest rates r increase call values by discounting future strike payments, while decreasing put values. Finally, expected cash dividends D depress post-dividend stock prices, which systematically damages call options and benefits put options.

hi.display: Interest Rates badhne se Call options expensive hote hain kyunki strike payment future mein discount hoti hai, jabki Puts cheaper hote hain. Expected Dividends stock price ko compress karte hain, isliye dividends Calls ko hurt karte hain aur Puts ko benefit karte hain.

scenes.title: Volatility Asymmetry: Why Volatility is an Option's Best Friend
scenes.purpose: Option owners have limited downside (capped at premium) but unlimited upside
takeaways: Option owners have limited downside (capped at premium) but unlimited upside
Higher volatility expands the distribution tails, boosting upside payoff probability
Extreme downside moves do not increase owner loss once the option is out of the money

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Among all six pricing variables, stock price volatility sigma exhibits a uniquely powerful characteristic. While equity investors generally avoid high volatility, option buyers actively seek it. Why does volatility always increase option value?

hi.display: Chhe factors mein se sabse fascinating factor hai Volatility yaani sigma. Volatility badhne par stock market investors nervous hote hain, lekin option buyers celebrate karte hain. Aisa kyun hota hai?

beats.onScreenIntent: Volatility Asymmetry: Why Volatility is an Option's Best Friend

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: The answer lies in Asymmetric Payoff Truncation. An option holder faces strictly capped downside risk: no matter how severely the underlying stock collapses, the holder's loss is limited to the initial premium paid.

hi.display: Iska reason hai Asymmetric Truncation. Option buyer ka maximum downside risk zero par permanently capped hota hai; chahe stock kitna bhi collapse ho jaye, buyer premium se zyada loss nahi kar sakta.

beats.onScreenIntent: Volatility Asymmetry: Why Volatility is an Option's Best Friend

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Conversely, favorable price movements possess unbounded upside. Higher volatility expands the right-tail probability of massive stock rallies without penalizing the truncated left-tail downside. Therefore, an increase in volatility strictly increases the fair value of both calls and puts.

hi.display: Lekin upside par koi cap nahi hota. Isliye jab volatility badhti hai aur extreme price swings ki probability badhti hai, toh positive right-tail payoff massively expand hota hai bina left-tail loss ko badhaye. Isliye higher volatility dono Calls aur Puts ki value ko strictly increase karti hai.

scenes.title: No-Arbitrage Upper Bounds: Calls and Puts
scenes.purpose: A call option can never be worth more than the underlying stock: c <= S0 and C <= S0
takeaways: A call option can never be worth more than the underlying stock: c <= S0 and C <= S0
If c > S0, an arbitrageur shorts the call and buys the stock, capturing risk-free cash upfront
A European put can never exceed K * exp(-rT); an American put can never exceed K

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Let us now formulate the mathematical boundary conditions that govern options pricing. We begin with the foundational Upper Bound: What is the absolute maximum theoretical price an option can ever command?

hi.display: Ab aate hain mathematical boundary conditions par. Pehla law hai: The Upper Bound. Ek option ki maximum theoretical price kitni ho sakti hai?

beats.onScreenIntent: No-Arbitrage Upper Bounds: Calls and Puts

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: For a call option, the upper bound is the current stock price S_0. Both European and American calls must satisfy c less than or equal to S_0, and C less than or equal to S_0. A contractual right to purchase an asset can never be worth more than the physical asset itself.

hi.display: Call option ka upper bound stock price S zero hota hai: small c and capital C are always less than or equal to S zero. Reason bilkul obvious hai: Kisi asset ko buy karne ka right us actual asset ke market price se zyada valuable kabhi nahi ho sakta.

beats.onScreenIntent: No-Arbitrage Upper Bounds: Calls and Puts

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: If a call ever traded above S_0, an arbitrageur would sell the call, buy the stock, and pocket risk-free profit immediately. For a European put, the maximum possible payoff at expiration is strike K, meaning its present value upper bound is K multiplied by e^(-rT).

hi.display: Agar koi call option stock price se mehanga quote hota hai, toh arbitrageur call sell karke immediately stock khareed lega aur risk-free cash difference pocket kar lega. European Put ka upper bound strike price ka discounted present value K e to the power minus rT hota hai kyunki maturity par maximum possible payout K dollars hota hai.

scenes.title: The Portfolio Dominance Method: Setting Up the Proof
scenes.purpose: Portfolio Dominance: If Portfolio A >= Portfolio B in all future states, then A0 must >= B0 today
takeaways: Portfolio Dominance: If Portfolio A >= Portfolio B in all future states, then A0 must >= B0 today
To prove call lower bounds, construct Portfolio A (Call + Cash K*exp(-rT)) and Portfolio B (1 share)
At maturity T, Portfolio A pays max(S_T, K), strictly dominating or matching Portfolio B (S_T)

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: To prove the minimum acceptable price—the Lower Bound—modern finance employs its most powerful analytical technique: The Portfolio Dominance Principle.

hi.display: Option ka Minimum Lower Bound prove karne ke liye quantitative finance ka sabse powerful theoretical tool use kiya jata hai: The Portfolio Dominance Principle.

beats.onScreenIntent: The Portfolio Dominance Method: Setting Up the Proof

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Let us construct two distinct investment portfolios today at time zero. Portfolio A consists of one European call option c plus a cash amount equal to K multiplied by e^(-rT) invested at the risk-free rate r. Portfolio B consists of one physical share of stock S_0.

hi.display: Aaiye do hypothetical portfolios construct karte hain. Portfolio A mein ek European Call option aur risk-free cash amount K e to the power minus r T shamil hai. Portfolio B mein simply ek share of stock S zero shamil hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: The Portfolio Dominance Method: Setting Up the Proof

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: The law of no-arbitrage states: If Portfolio A's terminal payoff is greater than or equal to Portfolio B's payoff in every possible future state of the world at maturity T, then Portfolio A must cost at least as much as Portfolio B today.

hi.display: No-arbitrage principle kehta hai ki agar maturity T par Portfolio A ka terminal payoff har possible market state mein Portfolio B se bada ya barabar hai, toh aaj inception par bhi Portfolio A ki present value Portfolio B se badi ya barabar honi chahiye.

scenes.title: Proof of the European Call Lower Bound: Hull Section 11.3
scenes.purpose: Since Portfolio A >= Portfolio B at T, initial cost A0 >= B0: c + K * exp(-rT) >= S0
takeaways: Since Portfolio A >= Portfolio B at T, initial cost A0 >= B0: c + K * exp(-rT) >= S0
Rearranging yields the lower bound: c >= S0 - K * exp(-rT)
Because an option price cannot be negative, c >= max(S0 - K * exp(-rT), 0)

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Let us trace the terminal cash flows at expiration date T on screen. Exactly two mutually exclusive market states can materialize.

hi.display: Screen par diye gaye mathematical proof ko follow kijiye. Maturity T par do possible scenarios ho sakte hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Proof of the European Call Lower Bound: Hull Section 11.3

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: In State One, if terminal stock price S_T exceeds strike K, the call is exercised. Portfolio A delivers S_T minus K from the option plus K from the cash investment, yielding S_T. Portfolio B delivers S_T. Both portfolios yield identical payoffs.

hi.display: Scenario One: Agar terminal stock price S T strike K se bada hota hai, toh Call exercise hogi. Portfolio A ki value banegi S T minus K plus cash K barabar S T. Portfolio B ki value bhi S T hai. Dono portfolios exactly equal hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Proof of the European Call Lower Bound: Hull Section 11.3

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: In State Two, if S_T is less than or equal to K, the call expires worthless. Portfolio A delivers cash K, while Portfolio B delivers stock worth S_T, which is strictly less than K. Portfolio A dominates in all states! Therefore, c plus K e^(-rT) must be greater than or equal to S_0, proving that c must be at least S_0 minus K e^(-rT).

hi.display: Scenario Two: Agar S T strike K se chhota ya barabar hai, toh Call expire worthless ho jayegi. Portfolio A ki value cash K rahegi, jabki Portfolio B ki value S T rahegi jo K se chhota hai. Portfolio A strictly jeet gaya! Isliye Portfolio A aaj bhi bada hona chahiye: c plus K e to the power minus rT is greater than or equal to S zero, proving c is greater than or equal to S zero minus K e to the power minus rT.

scenes.purpose: In Hull's example: S0 = $20, K = $18, r = 10%, T = 1 yr; Lower Bound = $3.71
takeaways: In Hull's example: S0 = $20, K = $18, r = 10%, T = 1 yr; Lower Bound = $3.71

At maturity, payoff is guaranteed risk-free profit of $0.71 in all market states

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Suppose market prices irrationally breach this boundary condition such that c falls below S_0 minus K e^(-rT). How does a quantitative trading desk exploit this mispricing to extract guaranteed profit?

hi.display: Agar market irrational ho jaye aur call option is lower bound ke neeche trade karne lage, toh trading desk par risk-free profit kaise lock kiya jata hai?

beats.onScreenIntent: Arbitrage Execution: Exploiting an Underpriced Call

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: In Step One, the desk buys the underpriced call at market price c, shorts one share of stock at spot price S_0, and invests the remaining net cash balance of S_0 minus c at the risk-free rate r.

hi.display: Step One: Underpriced call option ko cheap buy kijiye aur stock ko market mein spot price S zero par short sell kijiye. Step Two: Short sale se receive huye cash mein se call buy karke remaining cash ko risk-free rate r par invest kijiye.

beats.onScreenIntent: Arbitrage Execution: Exploiting an Underpriced Call

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: In Step Two, at maturity T, if S_T exceeds K, the desk exercises the call to acquire stock at strike K and closes its short position. The invested cash has grown to exceed strike K, leaving a risk-free net dollar surplus. Arbitrage buying immediately drives call prices back above the floor.

hi.display: Step Three: Maturity par agar stock strike se upar hai toh call exercise karke stock deliver kijiye. Agar stock strike ke neeche hai toh open market se cheap stock buy karke short cover kijiye aur cash interest pocket kijiye. Zero risk par upfront free money lock ho jati hai.

scenes.title: Lower Bound for European Puts on Non-Dividend Stocks
scenes.purpose: For European puts: p >= max(K * exp(-rT) - S0, 0)
takeaways: For European puts: p >= max(K * exp(-rT) - S0, 0)
Proof via Portfolio C (Put + Stock) vs Portfolio D (Cash K * exp(-rT))
Terminal value of Portfolio C is max(K, S_T), dominating Portfolio D (K)

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Applying the identical portfolio dominance methodology, John C. Hull derives the theoretical lower bound for a European put option on a non-dividend-paying stock.

hi.display: Exactly isi portfolio dominance method se John C. Hull European Put option ka minimum lower bound derive karte hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Lower Bound for European Puts on Non-Dividend Stocks

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Consider Portfolio C, consisting of one European put option p plus one share of stock S_0. Consider Portfolio D, consisting of cash K e^(-rT) invested at risk-free rate r.

hi.display: Portfolio C mein ek European Put option aur ek share of stock S zero shamil hai, jabki Portfolio D mein cash amount K e to the power minus r T shamil hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Lower Bound for European Puts on Non-Dividend Stocks

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: At maturity T, Portfolio C delivers max(S_T, K), which is always greater than or equal to K. Portfolio D delivers exactly K. Because Portfolio C dominates Portfolio D in every state, p plus S_0 must exceed K e^(-rT), proving that a European put must trade at or above K e^(-rT) minus S_0.

hi.display: Maturity par Portfolio C hamesha strike K ya stock price S T deliver karta hai, jo Portfolio D ke K dollars se bada ya barabar hota hai. Is derivation se prove hota hai ki European Put ki minimum floor barabar hoti hai: p is greater than or equal to maximum of K e to the power minus rT minus S zero, comma zero.

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: If an illiquid market allows a European put option to trade below this lower boundary condition, Reverse Cash-and-Carry Arbitrage is triggered immediately.

hi.display: Agar kisi illiquid market mein European put option is lower bound floor ke neeche trade hota hai, toh Reverse Arbitrage trigger hota hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Arbitrage Execution: Exploiting an Underpriced Put

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Step One: The trader buys the cheap put option at market price p and buys one share of stock at spot S_0, fully financing the combined purchase by borrowing cash from the money market.

hi.display: Step One: Underpriced put option buy kijiye aur underlying stock buy kijiye. Is purchase ko finance karne ke liye bank se cash borrow kijiye.

beats.onScreenIntent: Arbitrage Execution: Exploiting an Underpriced Put

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Step Two: At expiration T, the trader exercises the put if S_T is below K, selling the stock for strike K. Even in the worst-case scenario, the proceeds repay the borrowed money with interest and yield a positive cash profit.

hi.display: Step Two: Maturity T par agar stock strike se neeche rehta hai, toh put exercise karke stock ko guaranteed K dollars par sell kijiye aur loan repay karke positive cash spread lock kijiye. Market forces options ko instantly lower bound ke upar push kar deti hain.

scenes.title: Active Recall Scenario: Detecting Call Lower Bound Violations
scenes.purpose: Given S0 = $50, K = $45, r = 6%, T = 6 months (0.5 yrs): discount factor exp(-0.03) = 0.9704
takeaways: Given S0 = $50, K = $45, r = 6%, T = 6 months (0.5 yrs): discount factor exp(-0.03) = 0.9704
If market call trades at $5.50, it is underpriced by $0.83, creating pure arbitrage

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Let us now test your quantitative mastery of option lower bounds with a practical trading floor scenario. Carefully inspect the parameters displayed on screen.

hi.display: Chaliye ab ek practical lower bound arbitrage identification scenario solve karte hain. Screen par diye gaye parameters ko evaluate kijiye.

beats.onScreenIntent: Active Recall Scenario: Detecting Call Lower Bound Violations

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: A non-dividend stock trades at fifty dollars. The risk-free rate is five percent, and time to expiration is six months. A European call option with a strike price of forty dollars trades in the market for eight dollars and fifty cents. The discounted strike price is thirty-nine dollars and one cent. What is the theoretical lower bound, and what arbitrage profit is available? Pause and consider.

hi.display: Ek non-dividend stock fifty dollars par trade ho raha hai. Six-month risk-free rate five percent continuous hai. Forty dollar strike ka European call option market mein eight point five zero dollars par quote ho raha hai. Discounted strike price thirty-nine point zero one dollars hai. Lower bound kya hai aur kya arbitrage opportunity exist karti hai? Pause and consider.

beats.onScreenIntent: Active Recall Scenario: Detecting Call Lower Bound Violations

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: The correct answer is Option A: The lower bound is ten dollars and ninety-nine cents, and the call is underpriced by two dollars and forty-nine cents. S_0 minus K e^(-rT) equals fifty dollars minus thirty-nine dollars and one cent, which equals ten dollars and ninety-nine cents. Because the market price of eight dollars and fifty cents is less than ten dollars and ninety-nine cents, buying the call and shorting the stock locks in two dollars and forty-nine cents of risk-free arbitrage profit.

hi.display: Correct answer hai Option A: Lower bound ten point nine nine dollars hai; Call underpriced hai aur two point four nine dollars ka arbitrage profit exist karta hai. Calculation dekhiye: S zero fifty minus thirty-nine point zero one equals $10.99. Market price $8.50 lower bound $10.99 se kam hai. Call buy karke aur stock short karke instant $2.49 profit lock hota hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Active Recall Scenario: Detecting Call Lower Bound Violations

data.question: A stock trades at S0 = $50. A 6-month European call option has strike K = $45. The risk-free rate is 6% continuously compounded (exp(-0.03) = 0.9704). If the call trades at $5.50, is there an arbitrage opportunity, and what is the call lower bound?
options: The equilibrium condition holds via continuous risk-neutral replication.
Expected asset drift determines contingent claim value directly.
Arbitrage bounds can be systematically violated in liquid markets.
Discrete binomial tree steps eliminate all underlying price variance.
data.explanation: Lower bound = S0 - K*exp(-rT) = 50 - 45*0.9704 = 50 - 43.67 = $6.33. Because market price $5.50 < $6.33, the call violates the lower bound, creating an immediate risk-free arbitrage of $0.83.

scenes.title: Extension to Dividend-Paying Stocks: The Dividend Floor
scenes.purpose: When stock pays dividends with present value D, stock price S0 drops to S0 - D
takeaways: When stock pays dividends with present value D, stock price S0 drops to S0 - D
Adjusted European Call Lower Bound: c >= max(S0 - D - K * exp(-rT), 0)
Adjusted European Put Lower Bound: p >= max(D + K * exp(-rT) - S0, 0)

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: In real-world equity markets, common stocks pay periodic cash dividends. How do anticipated dividend distributions alter these fundamental lower boundaries?

hi.display: Real world mein stocks periodic cash dividends pay karte hain. Dividend-paying stocks par ye lower bounds kaise modify hote hain?

beats.onScreenIntent: Extension to Dividend-Paying Stocks: The Dividend Floor

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: John Hull demonstrates that the present value of all expected cash dividends D paid over the life of the option must be deducted from the current spot stock price S_0.

hi.display: Hull prove karte hain ki contract life ke dauran aane wale saare expected dividends ki present value D ko spot price S zero mein se subtract kiya jana chahiye.

beats.onScreenIntent: Extension to Dividend-Paying Stocks: The Dividend Floor

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: The dividend-adjusted lower bound for a European call becomes c greater than or equal to S_0 minus D minus K e^(-rT). Because dividend payouts remove cash from the firm and reduce post-dividend share prices, expected dividends systematically lower the call option price floor.

hi.display: Dividend-adjusted European call lower bound banta hai: c is greater than or equal to S zero minus D minus K e to the power minus r T. Dividend cash outflow stock price ko depress karta hai, isliye minimum call floor accordingly reduce ho jati hai.

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Let us consolidate our mastery of Chapter Eleven Part One through the four structural pillars of option boundaries.

hi.display: Aaiye Chapter Eleven Part One ke chaar foundational boundary principles ko consolidate karte hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Summary Thread: Four Pillars of Option Bounds & Arbitrage

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Pillar One: Factor Sensitivity Matrix. Volatility expands optionality for both calls and puts; interest rates enhance call values while reducing put values.

hi.display: Pillar One: Factor Sensitivity Matrix. Volatility dono Calls aur Puts ko badhati hai; rates calls ko help aur puts ko hurt karte hain.

en.display: Pillar Two: Unbreakable Upper Bounds. A call option can never exceed the underlying stock price; a European put can never exceed the present value of the strike.

hi.display: Pillar Two: Unbreakable Upper Bounds. Call option underlying stock se mehanga nahi ho sakta; put option discounted strike se bada nahi ho sakta.

en.display: Pillar Three: Portfolio Dominance Lower Bounds. No-arbitrage replication proves that European calls must trade at or above S_0 minus K e^(-rT).

hi.display: Pillar Three: Portfolio Dominance Lower Bounds. No-arbitrage replication non-dividend call par S zero minus K e to the power minus rT ki absolute floor enforce karta hai.

en.display: Pillar Four: Self-Enforcing Arbitrage. Price violations trigger immediate synthetic cash-and-carry replication, restoring market equilibrium.

hi.display: Pillar Four: Self-Enforcing Arbitrage. Bound violation hote hi market makers cash-and-carry style trading execute karke prices ko instantly equilibrium mein restore kar dete hain.
